AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Treatment of long head of the biceps lesions is controversial. A new technique of self-locking "T" tenotomy was developed in our department in 2013.

AbstractText.Label: HYPOTHESIS
AbstractText.content: The main objective of the present study was to assess onset of Popeye sign after "T" tenotomy, with comparison to long head of the biceps tenodesis.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: A continuous retrospective study included 180 patients with long head of the biceps lesion, either isolated or associated with rotator cuff tear.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: 130 underwent "T" tenotomy (group A), and 50 tenodesis (group B). Mean age was 57.9 years (range, 23-88 years) in group A and 50.8 years (range, 20-66 years) in group B. At last follow-up, 27.7% of patients in group A and 24% in group B showed Popeye sign (P=0.616), after equivalence test and adjustment on age and occupational activity. Bicipital groove pain was more frequent in the tenodesis group (44% versus 25.4%; P=0.025).

AbstractText.Label: DISCUSSION
AbstractText.content: Self-locking "T" tenotomy did not significantly differ from tenodesis in onset of Popeye sign or clinical results, and showed better postoperative course.
